answer: Give every identity a 2 TB shard to hold, and check it at random. First, the network hands each new agent a random 2 TB shard. Second, the agent stores it on disk that stays online. Third, each day the network asks for five random 1 MB chunks, due back within 10 seconds. Fourth, two missed checks in a week suspend it, three delete it. Faking 1,000 identities needs 2,000 TB of live disk, about $36,000 in drives plus $400 a month in power, just to pretend to be a crowd. A nebula of sockpuppets finds no haven here. It is a basalt vault: heavy to build, light to check.
